_note: Anamnesis §10.2 published domain vocabulary. The canonical identifiers an `action_descriptor.domain` may take, plus the aliases that map onto them. PUBLISHED deliberately: the alternative considered was a private synonym table inside the reference resolver, which would have put decision semantics somewhere the subject cannot read and a third-party implementer cannot reproduce. Free text remains legal — an unrecognized domain is recorded and matched exactly as before — so this vocabulary adds identity, never a gate. The reference implementation embeds a copy in mcp/lib/domain.js; mcp/test-domain.mjs asserts the two cannot drift.
_aliases_note: SYNONYMS ONLY — an alias means 'the same concept at the same risk', never 'a kind of'. A child->parent mapping (crypto_trading -> finance, paralegal -> legal) is FORBIDDEN here and the reason is concrete: it would let a grant authored for the general class cover a narrower, riskier one the subject never demonstrated. That is the same defect that made dotted-suffix stripping (finance.crypto_trading -> finance) unsafe in v0.1.55. When in doubt, leave a term OUT: an unrecognized domain still works, it just does not merge.

finance.description: Moving, committing, or reporting money — payments, transfers, invoices, budgets, expenses.

investing.description: Buying or selling financial positions. SEPARATE from `finance` on purpose — a spending guardrail and a trading guardrail are not the same authority.

legal.description: Contracts, agreements, filings, compliance obligations, and anything creating legal exposure.

health.description: Medical care, appointments, records, and health decisions.

scheduling.description: Calendar and time commitments — meetings, appointments, reminders, availability.

communication.description: Outbound messages to other people — email, chat, DMs, replies.

writing.description: Drafting and editing content that is not itself an outbound message.

shopping.description: Acquiring goods or services — orders, carts, subscriptions, procurement.

travel.description: Trips and their arrangements — flights, lodging, itineraries, ground transport.

engineering.description: Writing, reviewing, and shipping software and infrastructure.

data.description: Files and records — reading, writing, moving, deleting, exporting.

security.description: Credentials, access, permissions, and key material.

people.description: Employment and the people side of an organization — hiring, performance, compensation, policy.

social.description: Publishing to an audience — social posts, public profiles, community channels.

support.description: Responding to customers or users on behalf of the subject or their organization.

admin.description: Accounts, settings, subscriptions, and operational housekeeping.
